title: Most efficient way to fix bugs with Opus 5.5?
author: Pandaman_323
selftext:
Got a Claude pro sub for the first time last week and since then I’ve been loving it. However, I’m burning up my weekly usage in like 3 days.

I’m vibecoding some board games for fun that I’ve always to play on PC with rules automation and AI opponents. However, as the projects get more polished and refined, I find that even simple prompts like “fix this bug I just noticed” will eat up my usage.

Is there a more efficient way to debug that I am unaware of? Should I not have Claude Memory settings on and have it referencing some of my massive chat logs where I built the game (figured this would make it more efficient and lead to more more consistent results)?

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body: Consolidate your docs and open a new chat for each features or stage of development. Also, limit what each instance can see at a time. If you want to work on X and it depends only on Y and not Z, prompt it to only read relevant docs to X and Y, it'll save on the amount of tokens it ingests. Try and code during "sessions" (don't let more than 10 min to an hour between prompts) so you save by caching tokens.

comments.author: Intuition_Technology
comments.body:
Use something like superpowers. Use subagent driven development (to limit context per subagent).

Also instead of going bug by bug, ask Claude Opus to go through your code-base file by file, to identify bugs and write a plan to fix them.

Make sure to tell it to use only one subagent at a time, or 2 max or so, or you might hit your limit with 8 agents open, and lose all of their work.

Then just step through the plan.

Also useful might be to ask it to create an [Architecture.md](http://Architecture.md), in which it maps out what each part of your game does. Makes it easier for later agents to find what they need.

comments.author: faxt-orial
comments.body: Always ask claude to take notes in md files so it can use thwm further for faster navigation, also ask it to create automated tests, test coverage and the in-file notes/memory  helps in not going to far with debugging on usage . Also increases accuracy ( depends on the project and how its done ofc )

comments.author: Dicethrower
comments.body:
"<state problem>. Add logs to help you track the problem. Then after I run into the bug you analyse the logs."

Hasn't failed me yet.
